common_name: Zhuzhou Loropetalum (Tall Vigorous Purple-Leaf Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Zhuzhou grows considerably larger and faster than the many compact loropetalum cultivars now common in the trade, making it useful as a large screening shrub or small multi-trunked tree.

directions: Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade for the deepest foliage color. Zhuzhou is one of the larger, more vigorous loropetalum selections, growing into a substantial evergreen shrub or small tree rather than the low, compact mounds bred more recently for foundation plantings, making it valuable where a tall screen or specimen with the same rich burgundy-purple foliage and fringy hot-pink spring flowers is wanted. It flowers heavily in spring with a lighter rebloom possible later in the season, and the deep foliage color holds well through summer heat given adequate sun. It tolerates a range of soil conditions once established and needs only occasional structural pruning to maintain a strong framework as it reaches its larger mature size.

common_name: Clara Indian Hawthorn (Compact White-Flowered Indian Hawthorn)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring, summer, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Clara produces pure white flowers and a naturally compact, tidy habit that needs little pruning to stay in bounds.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun for the heaviest bloom, though it tolerates partial shade with somewhat reduced flowering. Clara is a compact Indian hawthorn selection valued for its clean white flower clusters in spring, a crisper look than the pink tones of most other cultivars, held against the same leathery, dark green, disease-resistant foliage typical of the species. Its naturally tidy, rounded size fits foundation plantings and low borders without the size Majestic Beauty or other larger selections eventually reach. Like other Indian hawthorns it is outstanding for coastal Gulf gardens, tolerating salt spray, wind, and poor sandy soil, and needs only a light shaping prune right after spring bloom.

common_name: Teddy Bear Magnolia (Compact Fuzzy-Backed Southern Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Teddy Bear is a compact, dense southern magnolia selection well suited to smaller residential lots where a full-sized Magnolia grandiflora would eventually overwhelm the space.

directions: Plant in moist, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Teddy Bear is a compact, densely pyramidal southern magnolia selection notable for its thick, glossy dark green leaves with dense, fuzzy cinnamon-brown undersides, a texture that gives the plant its name and provides striking contrast when wind or hand movement flips the leaves to show their reverse side. Its narrower, more upright form and smaller mature size than the massive straight species make it a practical evergreen specimen or screen for typical residential lots, while it still produces the large, fragrant, creamy white summer flowers magnolias are prized for. It requires little pruning to maintain its naturally tidy pyramidal shape and tolerates the same range of soil conditions as other southern magnolia selections.

common_name: Wine and Roses Weigela (Dark Purple-Leaf Pink-Flowered Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade; Wine and Roses holds its dark purple foliage color best with at least six hours of direct sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Wine and Roses was a breakthrough weigela introduction for combining rich, dark burgundy-purple foliage that holds its color through the growing season with abundant clusters of rose-pink, trumpet-shaped spring flowers that stand out sharply against the dark leaves. Hummingbirds are drawn strongly to the tubular flowers, and the plant provides months of foliage-color interest even after the main spring bloom flush ends. It is generally trouble-free, tolerating heat and average garden soil well, and needs only a light shaping prune right after flowering, since it blooms on the previous year's wood and heavy pruning at the wrong time removes the next season's flower buds.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade; Variegata holds its cream-edged foliage as a bright accent through the growing season, well after the spring flowers fade.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. A long-established classic among variegated shrubs, Variegata weigela produces soft green leaves broadly edged in creamy white that brighten a mixed border all season, paired with clusters of soft pink, trumpet-shaped flowers in late spring that draw hummingbirds. The variegated foliage provides ongoing visual interest well beyond the relatively brief flowering period typical of weigela cultivars. It performs best with a light shaping prune right after flowering, since blooms form on the previous year's wood, and is otherwise a tough, easy shrub tolerant of average soil and normal garden care.
